principles.text: Think about marketing before you commit any time to building.
Validate cheaply: put up a landing page, tweet it, and if nobody is interested, the product is broken.
Take one feature for one segment and make it better than the bloated incumbents.
Rent distribution by partnering with a creator; the audience, not the software, is the moat.
Treat products as stairs and plan an exit; selling a bootstrapped business gets you capital without raising.

sampleQA.question: How do I defend my SaaS when AI makes building trivial?

answer.text: Niche down. A narrow product is harder to replace than a general one.
Own or rent distribution: partner with a creator, because people buy the thing because it's theirs.
Solo he did $3-4k MRR; creator partnerships got him roughly 10x that.
VidAI, launched with a creator, did $14K on day one and $90K in month one.

sampleQA.question: Should I offer a free trial without a credit card?

answer.text: No-card trials drew a large number of phantom accounts exploiting the AI tools.
Requiring a card raised subscriptions and cut OpenAI usage.
Dropping trials for a 7-day refund policy raised revenue and kept only serious customers.
Prefer subscriptions: recurring revenue keeps paying when you pause marketing.

sampleQA.question: How do I get my SaaS ready to sell?

answer.text: Use Google Analytics; buyers distrust self-hosted analytics because the data can be faked.
If you depend on a platform, sell before it ships your feature itself.
Expect most buyers to be tire-kickers asking for MRR by month, calls and P&Ls.
He listed Morise on Acquire.com and sold it within a month.
